file_permission_mode.title: File Permission Mode (Octal)
file_permission_mode.description: The numeric octal permission mode of the sensitive file (e.g., 420 for 0644, 438 for 0666). World-readable modes expose the file to any local user.

file_classification.title: File Sensitivity Classification
file_classification.description: The type of sensitive content stored in the file, indicating whether it contains credentials, private keys, or sensitive configuration.

world_read_bit_set.title: World-Read Bit Set on File
world_read_bit_set.description: Whether the file has the world (other) read permission bit explicitly set, allowing any local user or process to read the file contents.

world_writable_paths_found.title: World-Writable Paths Detected
world_writable_paths_found.description: Indicates whether any critical directories or executable files have world-writable permissions (o+w), meaning any local user can modify them.

sticky_bit_missing_on_world_writable_dir.title: Sticky Bit Missing on World-Writable Directories
sticky_bit_missing_on_world_writable_dir.description: Indicates whether any world-writable directories lack the sticky bit, which normally prevents users from deleting or renaming files owned by others.

encryption_at_rest_enabled.title: Encryption at Rest Enabled
encryption_at_rest_enabled.description: Whether full-disk or volume-level encryption (e.g., LUKS, BitLocker, FileVault, dm-crypt) is enabled for the storage device or volume containing sensitive data.

filesystem_encryption_type.title: Filesystem Encryption Type
filesystem_encryption_type.description: The type of encryption mechanism applied to the filesystem or volume, if any. 'none' indicates no encryption is in use.

volume_contains_sensitive_paths.title: Volume Contains Sensitive Paths
volume_contains_sensitive_paths.description: Whether the unencrypted volume or filesystem hosts directories known to contain sensitive data such as /etc, /home, /var/lib, database data directories, credential stores, or application secret files.

key_storage_location.title: Encryption Key Storage Location
key_storage_location.description: Indicates whether encryption keys are stored on the same volume they protect, a separate volume, or an external key management system (KMS/HSM).

key_file_plaintext.title: Encryption Key Stored in Plaintext
key_file_plaintext.description: True if encryption key material is stored in plaintext (unencrypted) on the filesystem rather than in an encrypted or wrapped form.

key_file_permissions_octal.title: Key File Permission Octal
key_file_permissions_octal.description: The Unix permission octet string for the key file (e.g., '0640', '0644', '0777'). Permissions allowing group or world read/write indicate overly permissive access.

unauthorized_suid_sgid_binaries.title: Unauthorized SUID/SGID Binaries
unauthorized_suid_sgid_binaries.description: List of executable files with SUID or SGID bit set that are not in the organization-approved whitelist of binaries permitted to carry elevated execution bits.

suid_sgid_binaries_owned_by_root.title: Unauthorized SUID/SGID Binaries Owned by Root
suid_sgid_binaries_owned_by_root.description: Indicates whether any of the unauthorized SUID/SGID binaries are owned by root, making them direct privilege escalation paths to root-level execution.

world_writable_suid_sgid_binary_present.title: World-Writable SUID/SGID Binary Present
world_writable_suid_sgid_binary_present.description: Indicates whether any SUID or SGID binary is also world-writable, which would allow any user to replace the binary contents and then execute it with elevated privileges.

auditd_rules_configured.title: Auditd Rules Configured for Sensitive Paths
auditd_rules_configured.description: Whether auditd watch rules are present for sensitive files or directories (e.g., /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/ssh, /root).

auditd_service_running.title: Auditd Service Running
auditd_service_running.description: Whether the auditd daemon is currently active and running on the host.

sensitive_path_watch_count.title: Number of Sensitive Path Watch Rules
sensitive_path_watch_count.description: Count of auditd watch rules (-w) or inotify monitors targeting sensitive filesystem paths.

alternative_fs_monitoring_configured.title: Alternative Filesystem Monitoring Configured
alternative_fs_monitoring_configured.description: Whether a non-auditd filesystem monitoring solution (e.g., inotifywait, OSSEC, Wazuh FIM, Falco) is configured to monitor sensitive paths.

tmp_mount_options.title: Temporary Directory Mount Options (/tmp)
tmp_mount_options.description: The mount options applied to the /tmp filesystem as listed in /proc/mounts or mount output.

var_tmp_mount_options.title: /var/tmp Mount Options
var_tmp_mount_options.description: The mount options applied to the /var/tmp filesystem as listed in /proc/mounts or mount output.

log_file_permissions_world_readable.title: Log Files World-Readable
log_file_permissions_world_readable.description: Indicates whether log files are readable by all users (e.g., permissions such as 644, 664, 666, or world-readable ACLs), allowing unauthorized users to read log contents.

sensitive_data_patterns_in_logs.title: Sensitive Data Patterns Detected in Logs
sensitive_data_patterns_in_logs.description: Indicates whether log files contain patterns consistent with credentials, tokens, PII, or cryptographic material (e.g., passwords, API keys, SSNs, private keys).

log_sanitization_enabled.title: Log Sanitization / Redaction Enabled
log_sanitization_enabled.description: Indicates whether the application has log filtering or redaction mechanisms configured that scrub sensitive values before writing to log files.

fim_tool_installed.title: File Integrity Monitoring Tool Installed
fim_tool_installed.description: Whether a recognized file integrity monitoring tool (e.g., AIDE, Tripwire, Samhain, dm-verity) is installed on the system.

fim_monitoring_active.title: File Integrity Monitoring Actively Configured and Running
fim_monitoring_active.description: Whether an installed FIM tool is actively configured with a baseline database and scheduled or real-time monitoring of critical paths (e.g., /bin, /sbin, /lib, /etc).

fim_critical_paths_covered.title: Critical System Paths Covered by FIM Policy
fim_critical_paths_covered.description: Whether the FIM configuration explicitly covers critical system directories such as /bin, /sbin, /usr/bin, /usr/sbin, /lib, /lib64, /etc, and key configuration files.

noexec_option_set.title: noexec Mount Option Set
noexec_option_set.description: Indicates whether the 'noexec' mount option is present for the partition, preventing execution of binaries from that mount point.

nosuid_option_set.title: nosuid Mount Option Set
nosuid_option_set.description: Indicates whether the 'nosuid' mount option is present for the partition, preventing setuid/setgid bits from taking effect on executables.

nodev_option_set.title: nodev Mount Option Set
nodev_option_set.description: Indicates whether the 'nodev' mount option is present for the partition, preventing interpretation of character or block special devices.

plaintext_secrets_detected.title: Plaintext Secrets Detected on Filesystem
plaintext_secrets_detected.description: Indicates whether plaintext secrets (private keys, API tokens, passwords, certificates, or other credentials) have been found stored as unencrypted files on the filesystem.

secrets_manager_in_use.title: Secrets Manager or Encrypted Vault in Use
secrets_manager_in_use.description: Indicates whether the system or application is configured to retrieve secrets from a secrets manager or encrypted vault (e.g., HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, GCP Secret Manager) rather than reading them from local plaintext files.

secret_file_world_readable.title: Secret File is World-Readable
secret_file_world_readable.description: Indicates whether any detected plaintext secret file has permissions that allow reading by users other than the owning user or group (e.g., mode 644, 666, or 777).

root_owned_world_writable_path_count.title: Root-Owned World-Writable Path Count
root_owned_world_writable_path_count.description: Number of directories owned by root that also have world-writable (other write) permission bits set, making them exploitable by any local user.

root_owned_group_writable_path_count.title: Root-Owned Group-Writable Path Count
root_owned_group_writable_path_count.description: Number of directories owned by root where the group write bit is set and the group is not a tightly controlled privileged group, enabling group members to write into root-owned directories.

sticky_bit_enforced_on_writable_paths.title: Sticky Bit Enforced on World-Writable Paths
sticky_bit_enforced_on_writable_paths.description: Indicates whether all world-writable root-owned directories have the sticky bit set, which restricts deletion/rename to file owners and mitigates symlink and race-condition attacks.

disk_quota_enabled.title: Disk Quota Enforcement Enabled
disk_quota_enabled.description: Indicates whether disk quotas are enforced on the filesystem, restricting per-user or per-group disk usage to prevent space exhaustion.

quota_hard_limit_configured.title: Quota Hard Limit Configured
quota_hard_limit_configured.description: Indicates whether hard limits (absolute ceiling on disk usage) are configured for users or groups, preventing filesystem exhaustion even if soft limits are ignored.

kernel_has_known_cve.title: Kernel Has Known CVE
kernel_has_known_cve.description: Indicates whether the running kernel version is associated with one or more publicly disclosed CVEs affecting filesystem drivers or syscall handling (e.g., privilege escalation bugs).

days_since_last_kernel_update.title: Days Since Last Kernel Update
days_since_last_kernel_update.description: Number of days elapsed since the kernel package was last updated on the host.

live_kernel_patching_enabled.title: Live Kernel Patching Enabled
live_kernel_patching_enabled.description: Indicates whether a live kernel patching solution (e.g., kpatch, ksplice, livepatch) is active and applying security fixes without requiring a reboot.

backup_file_permission_mode.title: Backup File Permission Mode (Octal)
backup_file_permission_mode.description: The numeric (octal) Unix permission bits on the backup archive file (e.g., 644 = 0o644). Overly permissive modes allow unauthorized read access to sensitive backup content.

backup_contains_sensitive_data.title: Backup Contains Sensitive Data
backup_contains_sensitive_data.description: Whether the backup archive is known to contain sensitive material such as /etc/shadow, private key material, database credentials, or encryption keys.

backup_world_readable.title: Backup File is World-Readable
backup_world_readable.description: Whether the backup file has the world-readable (other read) permission bit set, meaning any local user can read the archive without needing elevated privileges.
